It was settled from Git, not from either file. The rebase is proven by ancestry: implementation commits 1331ed7d and 225a7b62 still exist as objects but are NOT ancestors of the head, the branch carries replayed commits 67d81537 and da2344cd with identical subjects, and d5cea027 (the merge of PR #2808) IS an ancestor of the head. Order: implement, rebase onto d5cea027, continue, then refresh by merge to 54e1e3c6. Both files now state this identically.

Generation 5 recorded head_sha 7663fe04 and evidenced all four checks 'at 7663fe04' -- a superseded head that no reviewer was reading -- and its contract recorded base_sha bfdb19c9, which is not this branch's merge base. head_sha is now 478c391b, the head this evidence commit describes and the head at which all four checks were actually run; base_sha is now 54e1e3c6, which is both the merge base and the pull request's base as GitHub reports it.

ACCURACY DEFECT RAISED BY REVIEW, CORRECTED IN PROSE ONLY: mode_sequence does not by itself stop an ordinary or merged stored instruction from dispatching at the workflow's mode input default of dry-run. Verified in the tree rather than accepted on the reviewer's word: the only non-test references to mode_sequence are its two producers (orchestrator-flow/reconcile.mjs:49 and manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:2084), so no consumer reads it back and refuses a dispatch on its value. For the ordinary and merged routes a dry-run is a required first phase and remains legal, so no lane exists to close. The single lane this change closes is the historical one, closed by the workflow's historical apply-only guard. The contract goal previously implied otherwise and has been corrected. No code was changed to make this true.

ACCURACY DEFECT RAISED BY REVIEW, RECORDED AS A KNOWN CONSEQUENCE: because occupancy is now judged on identity, persistInitialReady compares readyIdentityDigest instead of the stored bytes, so a ref carrying a CORRUPTED stored digest whose identity is otherwise identical now CONVERGES at persistInitialReady rather than failing there. The corruption is still caught, but later and elsewhere: terminalizeHistoricalPreviewReady re-derives the whole-record digest and refuses on the mismatch (manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:2094). Detection is deferred from the write path to the terminal path, not lost. This is the accepted price of letting the 117 pre-change refs converge, and it was deliberately NOT 'fixed' in code: narrowing the stored digest is exactly the generation-3 defect that two independent reviews rejected, so the whole-record stored digest stays.

THE SHIPPED DIGEST DESIGN IS UNCHANGED BY THIS GENERATION. Generation 3 narrowed the STORED digest to ready identity and both slots returned REVISE at head 20dabc75 (durable verdicts d7b36fff slot 1, 65d5945b slot 2), because consumers re-derive sha256(canonicalJson(<stored record>)) from the record they read back, so narrowing the writer would have repaired the 117 pre-change refs by making every newly written historical_rebind ref unreadable and fail-closing terminalization. Generation 4 kept the stored digest over the whole record and moved the compatibility concession into the occupancy check. This generation changes no code and leaves that design exactly as it stands.
